title: LRLS-v1.1: A Specification and Reference Simulation for Dual-Agent Exploration–Exploitation Under Hard Constraints
content: We present LRLS (Lobster RL Specification), a formal specification for constrained optimisation in which the classical exploration--exploitation trade-off is role-separated into two heterogeneous agent populations plus a scheduler. A high-entropy crayfish population generates coarse candidate habitats ("mud caves"); a low-entropy, constraint-aware Boston lobster population promotes candidates into verified feasible solutions ("reef gaps") via local refinement and constraint projection; a scheduler allocates population budgets, dispatches tasks and triggers global resampling. The specification fixes the state decomposition, six action primitives, a single reward structure \(r = r_{\mathrm{obj}} - \lambda_v C_v + \lambda_e \mathcal{H} - \lambda_m C_m\), a shared memory-pool schema, a four-stage training pipeline, seven mandatory reported metrics and a safety layer. We additionally describe v1.1 RoboZero, which maps the agents onto a heterogeneous robot fleet with a geometric embedding space, gossip-synchronised memory, multi-robot consensus voting and zero-shot transfer routes. To make the specification executable, we release a dependency-free deterministic reference simulation (single HTML file, 1100 ticks, \(22\times22\) reward terrain, 12 agents) and report illustrative single-run behaviour across four difficulty settings. This is a specification and a reference implementation, not a claim of algorithmic superiority. No learned policy, no multi-seed statistics, no baseline comparison and no physical-robot experiment are reported here; Section 6 states these limitations explicitly. The aim is to give the central hypothesis --- that a learned switching scheduler outperforms fixed temperature or entropy annealing --- a precise, reproducible target that can subsequently be falsified.
